Our Technology

ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant in Bangalore

ARTAS iX is a robotic hair-restoration system designed to assist experts during selected stages of hair transplantation. At NeoSculpt6, ARTAS technology is considered only after a detailed hair-loss, scalp and donor-area assessment.

How the Procedure Works

What Is ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration?

ARTAS iX uses robotic technology and a high-definition stereoscopic vision system to identify suitable hair follicular units from the scalp. The system can support experts during follicular-unit harvesting, recipient-site creation and implantation as part of a clinically planned hair-transplant procedure.

Treatment planning remains specialist led. The choice of technique depends on the pattern of hair loss, donor availability, scalp condition, hair characteristics and the result the patient hopes to achieve.

How Is ARTAS Different From Traditional Hair Transplant Procedures?

Traditional hair restoration procedures include Follicular Unit Transplantation (FUT) and manual Follicular Unit Excision (FUE). The appropriate method depends on the individual assessment and treatment plan.

  • 01

    Follicular Unit Transplantation (FUT)

    FUT involves removing a strip of scalp from the back of the head and separating the hair follicles from it for implantation into balding areas. Because it involves strip removal, FUT leaves a permanent linear scar, and some patients may experience scalp numbness, tingling, tightness or discomfort during recovery.

  • 02

    Manual Follicular Unit Excision (FUE)

    Manual FUE uses handheld instruments to extract individual hair grafts. The procedure relies on the expert’s or technician’s hand-eye coordination and involves repetitive graft extraction during surgery.

  • 03

    ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration

    ARTAS iX uses robotic technology to assist experts with precise and repetitive movements during follicular-unit harvesting. It is designed to identify suitable grafts, assist with extraction, create recipient sites and implant harvested follicles as part of the planned procedure.

Our Process

How Does the ARTAS iX Procedure Work?

The ARTAS iX high-definition stereoscopic vision system identifies grafts suitable for harvesting and provides detailed visualisation during the procedure.

The ARTAS iX harvesting system helps the expert dissect and harvest grafts from the donor area. Robotic technology supports consistent repetitive movements throughout this stage of the procedure.

After harvesting, the ARTAS iX system can create recipient sites according to the individual treatment plan, hairline design and graft-placement strategy.

ARTAS iX can support recipient-site making and implantation of harvested grafts. The treatment team plans every stage around the patient’s existing hair, donor area and restoration goal.

What Are the Benefits of ARTAS iX?

  • No Linear Scar

    ARTAS-assisted follicular-unit extraction does not use a strip-removal approach, so it does not create a linear donor scar.

  • No Plugs, Stitches or Staples

    The procedure is designed around individual follicular units rather than the plug-graft approach used in older transplant methods. It does not involve strip closure with stitches or staples.

  • Precise Graft Harvesting and Implantation

    Robotic technology supports detailed imaging, graft identification and repeatable procedural movements during the planned stages of treatment.

  • Natural-Looking Hair-Restoration Planning

    Hairline design, graft placement and density goals are planned around the individual’s facial proportions, existing hair, donor availability and long-term expectations.

Individual results, recovery experience and visible growth vary between patients.

Who Is ARTAS iX For?

  • Men and women with androgenetic alopecia

  • Hair and donor characteristics suitable for the technology-assisted procedure

  • Hair-loss pattern, donor area and scalp condition assessed first

ARTAS iX may be considered for men and women with androgenetic alopecia where hair and donor characteristics are suitable for the technology-assisted procedure. Hair-loss pattern, donor area, scalp condition and hair characteristics are assessed before treatment is recommended.

The expert determines whether ARTAS-assisted treatment is appropriate after evaluating the patient’s hair loss and donor area.

What Results Can You Expect From ARTAS iX?

Hair restoration develops gradually after treatment. Visible change is reviewed over time, with hair-transplant progress commonly assessed at different stages of the growth cycle. Actual growth, density, recovery and final appearance vary between patients.
